gita:2:1: The teaching begins where the breakdown is.
A man sat down in the middle of his life, eyes full of tears.
He had stopped being able to act.
That is the moment the voice beside him started speaking.
gita:2:2: This despair is not who you are.
Ask where it came from. It arrived; it was not always here.
It does not fit you. It costs you your honor.
And it shuts the door you were walking toward.
gita:2:3: Do not hand your strength over to weakness.
It does not suit you. It never did.
Shake off the small faintness in your heart.
gita:2:4: How do you act against the people who raised you?
Arjuna looked across the field and saw his teacher.
He saw the elder he had bowed to since he was a boy.
And he asked how a man is supposed to aim at them.
gita:2:5: Some victories are not worth what they cost.
Better to live on alms than to cut down your own teachers.
Win that way and every pleasure you buy is stained.
gita:2:6: You cannot always tell which outcome is the good one.
Winning here and losing here look equally unbearable.
The people you do not want to harm are standing in front of you.
gita:2:7: There is a point where you stop being able to decide.
Pity has clouded the mind that used to know its duty.
Then the only honest sentence left is: teach me.
Ask, and mean it. That is where instruction begins.
gita:2:8: No amount of winning would fix this.
Give him the whole earth. Give him a throne among the gods.
The grief burning through his senses would still be there.
gita:2:9: He said it plainly: I will not fight.
The refusal took three words. The silence lasted longer.
gita:2:10: He was breaking down. The answer came smiling.
Two armies waiting. One man sunk in despair between them.
And the voice beside him was not alarmed at all.
gita:2:11: You are grieving for what was never lost.
Your words sound wise. Your sorrow says otherwise.
The wise do not mourn the living or the dead.
gita:2:12: There was never a time you were not.
Not you. Not me. Not one of these people standing here.
And there will never be a time when we stop.
gita:2:13: You already survived being a child.
The boy is gone. The young man is gone. You are still here.
The body kept changing and something did not.
Death is one more change of that kind. The steady do not flinch.
gita:2:14: Cold passes. Heat passes. So does this.
Pleasure and pain come from contact, and contact does not last.
Everything that arrives is already on its way out.
Learn to sit through them without flinching.
gita:2:15: The one these things cannot shake is the one who lasts.
Pleasure comes; he does not lean in. Pain comes; he does not break.
Same man in both. That is what makes him fit for the deathless.
gita:2:16: Everyone who has looked closely has reported the same thing.
gita:2:17: Something in all of this cannot be destroyed.
It spreads through everything you can see.
No power anywhere has ever managed to end it.
gita:2:18: Bodies end. What wears them does not.
The one inside cannot be measured or destroyed.
Knowing that, stand up and do what is yours to do.
gita:2:19: The one who thinks he kills is mistaken.
So is the one who thinks he can be killed.
That which you are does neither.
gita:2:20: You were not born. You do not die.
Nothing about you began, so nothing about you can end.
Unchanging. Older than anything you can name.
When the body is killed, it is not touched.
gita:2:21: Once you know it cannot be destroyed, whom would you kill?
The man who has seen that cannot be a slayer, or make one.
gita:2:22: You change clothes without mourning them.
Worn out, so you set them down and put on new ones.
The one who wears the body does exactly this.
gita:2:23: No blade has ever reached it.
Fire cannot burn it. Water cannot soak it.
Wind blows over it and takes nothing away.
gita:2:24: Nothing in the world can get at it.
Not cut, not burned, not soaked, not dried.
Everywhere at once. Steady. Older than time.
gita:2:25: It does not show itself, and it does not change.
The mind cannot picture it, however hard you try.
gita:2:26: Suppose you are right, and it does die.
Suppose it is born again and again, endlessly.
Even then there is nothing here worth your grief.
gita:2:27: Everything born dies. Everything that dies is born.
Neither half of that is news.
Do not spend your life grieving what was never avoidable.
gita:2:28: You did not see them arrive.
For a while they are here, in the middle of things, visible.
Then they are out of sight again.
What exactly is there to grieve?
gita:2:29: Everyone calls it a wonder. Almost no one knows it.
One man glimpses it. Another describes it. A third listens.
And still, having heard, they do not understand.
gita:2:30: The one inside every body cannot be destroyed.
Not yours. Not the stranger's. Not any creature alive.
So grieve for none of them.
gita:2:31: Look at your own duty and stop wavering.
You were made for a certain kind of work.
For the one who defends what is right, nothing is higher.
gita:2:32: Some doors open on their own.
You did not go looking for this fight. It arrived.
Count yourself fortunate when the right work comes to find you.
gita:2:33: Walking away has a price too.
Refuse the fight that is rightly yours and you abandon your duty.
You lose your name with it, and the fault is yours.
gita:2:34: They will tell this story for a long time.
For a man who has been honored, disgrace cuts deeper than dying.
That is what one refusal can buy.
gita:2:35: They will not call it wisdom. They will call it fear.
The men who fought beside you will read it that way.
The ones who thought most of you will think least.
gita:2:36: Your enemies will make a joke of your strength.
They will find words for it you will have to hear.
Tell me what hurts more than that.
gita:2:37: Either way, you do not lose.
Fall, and heaven is yours. Stand, and the earth is.
So get up, and settle it.
gita:2:38: Make winning and losing weigh the same.
Pleasure and pain. Gain and loss. Put them on one level.
Then act, and the act leaves no stain on you.
gita:2:39: The other half is how you work.
Hold both, and what you do stops binding you.
gita:2:40: Nothing you put in here is wasted.
No effort lost. No damage done. Nothing turned against you.
Even a little of this carries you through great fear.
gita:2:41: One decision beats a thousand opinions.
The steady mind runs on a single resolve.
The unsettled mind branches forever and arrives nowhere.
gita:2:42: Beautiful words are not the same as truth.
Some people fall in love with the promises in the text.
They quote the flowering parts and say there is nothing more.
gita:2:43: They want heaven, and they want it for the pleasure.
Every rite they teach is aimed at enjoyment and power.
So the works keep going, and so do the births.
gita:2:44: You cannot chase pleasure and settle the mind.
Attached to enjoyment and standing, the mind is always pulled.
It never sets into the one steady conviction that holds.
gita:2:45: Rise above the pairs that keep pulling you.
Hot and cold. Praise and blame. Stop being decided by them.
Stop calculating what to get and what to keep.
Stand in what is steady in you.
gita:2:46: When the flood arrives, who needs the well?
A tank of water is precious until water is everywhere.
That is what the scriptures become to a man who has known the Self.
gita:2:47: Do the work. Release the outcome.
The action is yours. What comes of it never was.
Do not let the reward become the reason.
And do not use that as an excuse to do nothing.
gita:2:48: Work steady, and let the result land where it lands.
Succeed or fail, you stay the same size.
That evenness has a name. It is called yoga.
gita:2:49: Working for the reward is the poorest way to work.
Action driven by the fruit sits far below action guided by wisdom.
Take shelter in the understanding, not in the payoff.
gita:2:50: Meet the world with an even mind and you shed credit and blame.
Good deed and bad deed alike stop sticking to you.
This is a discipline. Give yourself to it.
gita:2:51: Let go of the fruit and the chain comes off.
The wise release what their work will earn them.
Freed from birth itself, they reach the place where nothing harms.
gita:2:52: One day the confusion thins out.
Your mind climbs out of the mud it has been standing in.
Then what you have been told, and what you have yet to hear, lose their grip.
gita:2:53: You have read enough. Now stand still.
The mind that the texts have pulled in every direction settles.
It rests in the Self, unmoving. That is the arrival.
gita:2:54: How would you recognize such a person?
Arjuna asked the practical question: what does he sound like?
How does he sit? How does he walk down a street?
gita:2:55: He wants nothing, and he is not lacking.
Every desire the mind kept manufacturing has been set down.
He is content in himself, by himself. That is steady wisdom.
gita:2:56: Trouble comes and his mind does not move.
Good times come and he does not go hunting for more.
No clinging. No fear. No anger. That is the settled one.
gita:2:57: Good news, bad news. Same face.
He meets both without holding on to either.
He does not celebrate and he does not recoil. His wisdom is firm.
gita:2:58: Watch a tortoise pull everything in.
Head, legs, all of it, drawn back under the shell.
Do that with your senses when they reach for the world.
That is when wisdom holds still.
gita:2:59: Starve a craving and it still waits for you.
You can drop the object and keep the taste for it.
Only seeing the highest takes the taste away too.
gita:2:60: The senses are violent, and they do not respect your effort.
A man can be striving hard and still be carried off.
gita:2:61: Gather them all in, and sit down.
Hold the senses; keep your attention on the highest.
The one whose senses obey him is the one whose wisdom holds.
gita:2:62: Don't follow every thought you get.
Keep circling an object and you get attached to it.
And desire, blocked, turns into anger.
gita:2:63: Anger is where the fall starts.
Anger clouds you. Clouded, you forget what you knew.
Forgetting, you lose the power to tell right from wrong.
gita:2:64: You can live among all of it and stay clear.
Keep moving through the world. Keep hold of your senses.
Nothing pulling you in, nothing pushing you away.
That is what peace is made of.
gita:2:65: In that peace, the ache stops.
Every sorrow you carried loses its hold.
And the calm mind settles quickly into steadiness.
gita:2:66: No steadiness, no peace. No peace, no happiness.
The scattered mind cannot know anything truly.
It cannot settle, so it never finds quiet.
And nobody has ever been happy without quiet.
gita:2:67: One sense pulls, and the whole mind goes with it.
Your judgment goes with the mind.
Wind on open water takes the boat wherever it likes.
gita:2:68: Hold the senses and the knowing holds.
Everything rests on that one restraint.
Draw them back from what they reach for, completely.
gita:2:69: He is awake in what puts everyone else to sleep.
What the world calls night is where he sees clearly.
What the world is busy chasing is darkness to him.
gita:2:70: Rivers pour in all day. The ocean does not rise.
Let desires arrive like that and you stay level.
The man who runs after them never does.
gita:2:71: Walk through the world owning nothing.
Desires set down. Nothing you are reaching for.
No mine. No I. That is the man at peace.
gita:2:72: This is the state that does not come and go.
Reach it and delusion no longer finds a way in.
Stand in it, even at the last hour, and you are one with the whole.
gita:3:8: Take up the work that is actually yours.
You could not even keep this body alive by sitting still.
gita:3:16: Take no part in it, and take your pleasure only in the senses.
Then you have spent a life on nothing.
gita:3:19: Do what should be done, without gripping it.
Always. Not when you feel like it.
Work held loosely is the road that goes all the way up.
gita:3:21: People are watching how you do it.
Whatever the respected man does, the rest take up.
Whatever he treats as normal becomes the standard.
gita:3:27: You are not the one doing this.
Nature's own forces carry out every action there is.
Only the ego stands up afterward and says: that was me.
gita:3:30: Put the work down at his feet, then fight.
Mind on what is real in you. No expectation. No self-display.
gita:3:35: Your own work, done badly, beats another's done well.
Live your life, not the one that looks better from here.
Better to die in your own duty.
The other man's road is full of danger for you.
gita:3:37: Here is the enemy. It is desire.
And behind desire, its shadow: anger.
Both born of restlessness. Both bottomless.
That is what you are actually fighting.
gita:3:42: There is an order to what is in you.
The senses stand above the body. The mind above the senses.
And above the intellect, the one you actually are.
gita:3:43: Steady yourself with what is highest in you.
Know the one that stands above even your reason.
Then kill the enemy called desire.
It is hard to beat. Do it anyway.
gita:4:7: When what is right thins out, he arrives.
Whenever wrong starts to spread and take the room.
That is the moment he takes form.
gita:4:8: To protect the good. To end the cruel.
To set what is right back on its feet.
For that, he says, he is born in every age.
gita:4:11: However you come to him, that is how he meets you.
The answer takes the shape of the asking.
Every road men walk is finally his.
gita:4:18: See the stillness inside your own doing.
And see the doing hidden inside stillness.
The man who sees both is the wise one.
gita:4:20: Busy all day, and untouched by it.
He gave up any claim on what the work would bring.
So he acts, and nothing is being done.
gita:4:24: The offering, the fire, and the hand that pours.
All of it is the same one thing.
See that in what you are doing, and that is where you arrive.
gita:4:34: Go to someone who has actually seen it.
Bow. Ask honestly. Serve without keeping score.
Knowledge is handed over that way, and not another.
gita:4:38: Nothing cleans a man like knowing.
There is no purifier anywhere to match it.
Stay with the practice and you find it inside yourself.
gita:4:39: Faith, focus, and a hand on the senses.
That is who this knowledge comes to.
And once it comes, peace does not keep you waiting.
gita:4:42: Cut the doubt out of your own heart.
It was never anything but ignorance sitting there.
Knowledge is the blade. Use it.
Then take your stand, and get up.
gita:6:5: Lift yourself. No one else can.
And do not be the one who drags you down.
You are your own friend here.
You are also the only enemy who never leaves.
gita:6:6: Win yourself over and you have an ally for life.
Lose to yourself and the same self turns on you.
It behaves exactly like an enemy outside you.
gita:6:16: Extremes will cost you the practice.
Not for the man who overeats, and not for the one who starves.
Not for the one who sleeps all day, or never sleeps.
gita:6:17: Moderation is not a small virtue.
Measured in what you eat and how you rest.
Measured in your work and in your sleeping hours.
Live that way, and the practice starts taking your pain apart.
gita:6:19: A flame indoors does not flicker.
No wind reaching it, so it stands perfectly still.
That is the mind that has been gathered in.
gita:6:26: Wherever it wanders off to, bring it back.
The mind is restless. It will keep leaving.
That is the whole instruction: notice, and return it.
gita:6:30: See him everywhere and you are never apart.
Everything held in him. Him in everything.
The man who sees that is never lost to him, nor he to the man.
gita:6:35: Yes, the mind is hard to hold.
Restless, he agreed, and difficult. He did not argue.
Then he named the two things that work.
Practice, and letting go of what you crave.
gita:6:40: No one who does good comes to a bad end.
Not in this life, not in whatever follows it.
Nothing you build that way is destroyed.
gita:6:47: Of all of them, one stands closest.
The one whose inner self has gone into him.
Full of faith, and turned that way without reserve.
gita:7:3: Out of thousands, one even tries.
Of the ones who try and get somewhere, one truly knows him.
That is the honest count. Now decide.
gita:7:7: Everything you see is strung on him.
Like beads on a thread you cannot see.
gita:7:14: The illusion is real enough to drown in.
It is made of the three qualities and it is his own.
No one crosses it by force.
The ones who take refuge in him get across.
gita:7:16: Four kinds of people come to him.
The one in trouble. The one who wants to understand.
The one who wants something. And the one who knows.
All four are counted among the good.
gita:7:19: It takes most people many lifetimes.
At the end of them, the wise man arrives.
He has seen that all of this is one thing.
Such a soul, he says, is very hard to find.
gita:9:22: Look at one thing only, and you are carried.
For those who hold to him without dividing their attention.
He brings what they do not have.
And he keeps safe what they do.
gita:9:26: A leaf is enough. A little water is enough.
A flower, a piece of fruit, offered with devotion.
From a clean heart, he says, he accepts it.
gita:9:27: Whatever you do, do it as an offering.
What you eat. What you give away.
What you sacrifice. What you go without.
All of it can be handed over as it happens.
gita:9:29: The same toward every living thing. None hated, none preferred.
But those who turn toward him with love are in him.
gita:9:30: Even the worst man can turn.
If he gives himself to this and to nothing else.
Count him among the good from that moment.
He has decided rightly, and that is what counts.
gita:9:34: Give it your mind. Give it your heart.
Offer to him. Bow to him.
Bind your whole self there and set nothing above it.
gita:12:1: Should you worship a face, or the formless?
Some fix their hearts on you, steady, every day.
Others reach for what has no form at all.
Arjuna asked which of the two knows yoga better.
gita:12:2: The ones who never look away.
Mind fixed on the highest, day after day, without drifting.
Faith at full strength behind it.
Those, he said, are the finest at this.
gita:12:3: Some worship what cannot be pictured.
No name for it. No form. Nothing the mind can hold.
Everywhere at once. Unmoving. Without end.
gita:12:4: Hold your senses. Be the same wherever you stand.
And want the good of every living thing.
Those who do reach him too.
gita:12:5: The formless path is the harder road.
You have a body, and a body struggles to hold what has no shape.
gita:12:6: Hand the work over and keep your eyes on one thing.
Every action laid down at his feet.
Nothing else set above him. Nothing else in the mind.
gita:12:7: Set your mind there and you will be lifted out.
This life is an ocean, and people go under in it.
He says he comes quickly for the ones who are looking at him.
gita:12:8: Put your mind here. Put your reason here.
Not one, then the other. Both.
Do that and there is nowhere else you will live.
gita:12:9: Cannot hold your mind steady? Then practice.
He does not lose patience with you for failing at the first thing.
Come back to it, again and again. That is the second road.
gita:12:10: Cannot keep even the practice? Then work for him.
Do the ordinary things, but do them for his sake.
That alone will carry you the whole way.
gita:12:11: And if you cannot manage that either.
Take refuge in him and give up what your work earns you.
Hold yourself steady and let the fruit go.
There is always a lower step. He keeps building them.
gita:12:12: There is a ladder, and the top rung is letting go.
Knowing beats drilling. Meditation beats knowing.
And giving up the fruit beats meditation.
Peace does not come later. It follows immediately.
gita:12:13: He hates nothing that is alive.
Friendly to all of it. Sorry for its suffering.
No grasping, no self-importance, steady in pleasure and pain.
gita:12:14: Content always. Not only when things go well.
Steady in practice. In command of himself.
Certain of what he has decided, mind and reason given over.
That one, he says, is dear to me.
gita:12:15: He disturbs no one, and no one disturbs him.
The world does not set him off, and he does not set it off.
Free of elation, anger, fear, and worry.
That one is dear to me.
gita:12:16: He needs nothing, and he does his work well.
Clean, capable, unbothered, carrying no ache.
He has stopped launching things for his own sake.
That one is dear to me.
gita:12:17: Nothing thrills him. Nothing sours him.
He does not grieve and he does not crave.
Good fortune and bad, he has set both down.
gita:12:18: Same to the friend and to the enemy.
Praised or shamed, he is the same man.
Cold or heat, pleasure or pain, he does not change size.
Nothing has a hook in him.
gita:12:19: Praise and blame land the same way.
He keeps quiet. He is content with whatever comes.
No fixed place he must live. No wavering in him.
That man is dear to me.
gita:12:20: Follow this, and you are held closest of all.
The teaching he has just given does not die.
Take it up with faith, with him as the one aim.
Those, he says, are dearest to me.
gita:15:1: There is a tree with its roots in the sky.
Its branches grow downward, into this world.
Its leaves are the hymns men sing.
Know that tree and you know the scriptures.
gita:15:5: Pride gone. Delusion gone. Clinging beaten.
Living in what is real in you, with the wanting turned away.
No longer thrown between pleasure and pain.
That is who reaches the goal that does not end.
gita:15:7: A piece of the eternal is walking around in you.
It became a living soul in this world.
It gathers the five senses to itself, and the mind as the sixth.
And it lives here, inside nature.
gita:15:15: He is sitting in every heart, including yours.
Memory comes from there. So does knowing.
So does the losing of both.
Everything the scriptures point at is pointing there.
gita:18:14: Nothing you do, you do alone.
Every act needs a body to happen in, and someone to claim it.
It needs the senses, and effort of many kinds.
And a fifth thing, which is not yours at all.
gita:18:23: There is a clean way to do a thing.
It is the work that was yours to do.
Done without clinging, without love or hate in it.
And without one eye on the reward.
gita:18:47: Do your own work, even badly.
A flawed duty of your own beats another man's, well done.
Follow the work your nature was cut for.
Nothing you do there will stain you.
gita:18:48: There is no undertaking anywhere without some fault in it.
So do not walk away from the work you were born to.
Waiting for a clean one is waiting forever.
gita:18:56: You can keep working and still be carried.
Take refuge in him and go on doing everything.
By his grace you reach what does not end.
gita:18:58: Keep your mind here and the walls come down.
By his grace, every obstacle is passed.
Refuse to listen because your pride is loud, and you are lost.
gita:18:61: He is in the heart of every being.
And by his power all of them are turned.
Mounted on a machine, going round.
gita:18:63: Now think it over. Then do as you like.
He gave the deepest thing he had to give.
And then he handed the decision back.
gita:18:66: Set it all down. Come to me.
Every duty, every rule you have been carrying.
I will free you from everything you have done wrong.
gita:18:78: Where those two stand together, it is settled.
The one who knows, and the one who acts.
There you find fortune, victory, and steady ground.
That, says the man who watched it, is certain.
